units.label: Browser
units.role: End user's browser; requests pages and submits form posts.

units.label: Next.js server
units.role: Next.js 15 App Router process: page server-components and /api route handlers.

units.label: Postgres
units.role: Primary store for the orders table; queried directly via postgres-js tagged templates.

units.label: Stripe
units.role: External payment processor that POSTs signed webhook events to /api/webhooks/stripe.

flows.title: User opens the orders page
flows.name: User opens the orders page
flows.tagline: GET /orders → server component SELECTs and renders the HTML.
flows.narration: The user requests /orders. The server component reads the 50 most recent rows from Postgres, renders the HTML on the server, and returns the streamed response.

steps.narration: The browser requests /orders. Next routes the request into the OrdersPage server component.

steps.payload: SELECT id, customer_id, amount_cents, currency, created_at FROM orders ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50
steps.narration: The server component awaits the tagged-template query inside its body. The page does not return until the rows are in memory.
Postgres returns the matching rows. The component continues, mapping each row through OrderList.

steps.payload: Streaming HTML response with the rendered orders table.
steps.narration: Next streams the rendered HTML back. The browser parses it and paints the orders table.

flows.title: Client POSTs a new order
flows.name: Client POSTs a new order
flows.tagline: POST /api/orders → row inserted → 201 with the new id.
flows.narration: A client POSTs a JSON body to /api/orders. The route validates with Zod, inserts a row, and returns 201 with the generated id.

steps.narration: The form posts JSON to /api/orders. The handler parses and validates against the OrderCreate schema.

steps.payload: INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, amount_cents, currency, status) VALUES (...) RETURNING id
steps.narration: The route runs the INSERT and reads back the new id via RETURNING.
Postgres returns the inserted row. The route uses only the id field.
The route serialises the id into JSON and returns 201.

flows.title: Stripe webhook fires
flows.name: Stripe webhook fires
flows.tagline: Stripe POSTs an event; the route verifies the signature and updates the order.
flows.narration: Stripe POSTs a signed event to /api/webhooks/stripe. The route verifies the stripe-signature header against the webhook secret and updates the matching order row when the event is payment_intent.succeeded.

steps.payload: POST /api/webhooks/stripe header stripe-signature=<sig> body: raw event JSON
steps.narration: Stripe sends the event with the stripe-signature header set. Next pipes the raw body in so the signature check sees the exact bytes Stripe signed.
The route calls constructEvent to verify the signature. A bad signature returns 400 immediately without touching the database.

steps.payload: UPDATE orders SET status = 'paid' WHERE stripe_pi_id = <pi.id>
steps.narration: For payment_intent.succeeded events the route runs an UPDATE on the matching order row.
The route returns 200 with a small JSON body so Stripe records the event as delivered.

glossary.Server component: A Next.js 15 component that executes on the server and renders to HTML; it can await database calls inside its body.
glossary.API route: A route handler under app/api that returns JSON; runs server-side per request.
glossary.Webhook: An inbound HTTP POST from an external system carrying an event payload.
glossary.Signature verification: Comparing an HMAC of the raw request body against a header value to confirm the sender and rule out tampering.
glossary.Zod: A TypeScript schema library used here to parse incoming JSON bodies before they touch the database.
